title: Consolidate Console Insights: MVP metric set, phased rollouts, and acceptance
creator: Asha Patel
description: Trim the initial Console Insights surface to a minimal, high-value subset so we can ship a reliable first iteration within the next sprint. This ticket captures the scope reductions, acceptance criteria, rollout strategy, and trade-offs for dashboards, tracing links, and route-level cost breakdowns. Aim: deliver a stable, well-instrumented baseline that meets critical customer needs (top cost drivers + basic trace navigation) while deferring lower-value/expensive features (per-token cost drilldowns, full-span flamegraphs, heavy sampling for traces).
background: Multiple PM and engineering reviews have identified that the original Console Insights scope is too broad for the next release. Backend query costs and frontend performance concerns threaten SLA commitments. Customers primarily ask for: (1) clear top-level cost drivers by route/model, (2) quick navigation from a cost item to a representative trace, and (3) lightweight daily aggregations rather than live streaming of all metrics. This ticket establishes the MVP cuts and an execution plan to de-risk launch.
goals: Deliver a Console Insights MVP that surfaces top cost drivers (top 5) per account/routes per day
Provide a single-click link from cost item to a representative trace (not full trace explorer)
Keep backend query costs predictable with aggregated windows and sampling targets
Enable phased rollout with feature flags and canary to dedicated customers before GA
out_of_scope: Per-token or per-request full cost breakdowns (deferred)
Full span-level flamegraphs and heavy trace sampling (deferred)
Long retention for raw telemetry in the initial release (deferred to retention-add-on)
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows top 5 cost drivers for last 24h and last 7d with stable load times (<1.5s for common queries)
Each cost item includes a 'View trace' link that opens a representative trace in the Console with log link preserved
Backend aggregated queries operate at daily/hourly windows and keep additional query cost under the allocated budget (SLO: < 10% added telemetry spend for initial rollout)
Rollout plan implemented via flags allowing 0%, 10%, 50%, 100% cohorts and manual rollback
E2E tests cover dashboard rendering, trace link correctness, and feature flag gates
Documentation and an admin FAQ shipped with console-2025.03 release notes
tradeoffs_and_risks: Limiting to top 5 drivers reduces noise but may hide smaller but critical anomalies
Representative trace approach speeds rollout but may not reproduce rare failure modes
Aggregated windows reduce backend cost but reduce fidelity for debugging short spikes
Deferring long retention slows long-tail investigations for customers on day-one
